A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViTime/RealTS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, with corresponding content identifiable despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original ViTime zero-shot forecasting, fine-tuning and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original forecasting results and adds robustness experiments, additional ablations, attention visualizations and computational-resource measurements.

M1.justification: The RealTS generator, mappings and tokenizer/decoder/refiner architecture are retained. However, v3 Table 6 labels the proposed loss JSD+EMD, while Equation (10) retains the EMD+KLD objective from v2 Equation (15). The PDFs do not resolve whether the loss changed or the ablation was mislabeled.

E1.justification: The seven benchmark datasets and RealTS training coverage remain. V3 substantially expands evaluation conditions to include Gaussian noise, added harmonics and missing observations (Section 4.4 and Appendix E.4), extending coverage beyond the original forecasting and temporal-rescaling scenarios.

E2.justification: The main zero-shot and fine-tuning comparator sets are retained. However, v3 Table 8 contains TIME-LLM entries for Electricity, Traffic and Weather where v2 reported none. These duplicate v2's supervised PatchTST values, while v3 Table 2 still marks TIME-LLM results unreported. Actual comparator participation in these cases is therefore ambiguous.

E3.justification: Existing lookback lengths, forecast horizons and rescaling metrics are retained. New protocols include Gaussian-noise standard deviations of 0.1 and 0.3, missing-data rates spanning 10–90%, intermediate fine-tuning proportions, MS and loss-component sweeps, and inference profiling with batch size 4 on a single NVIDIA 3090.

E4.justification: The original resolution, lookback and model-size studies remain in v3 Figure 14. V3 adds MS and loss ablations, a refining-module comparison, corruption tests, fine-tuning and missing-data sweeps, Grad-CAM/attention analyses, and an explosive-growth case study. V2's Weather forecast illustrations are omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions use error bars and shaded bands without specifying their statistical interpretation. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval definitions or significance tests. Additional plots using similar bands do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Reported ViTime zero-shot values change substantially: mean ETTh1 ReMSE changes from 0.539 to 0.490, while Traffic changes from 0.726 to 0.760 (v2 Table I; v3 Table 7). V3 also corrects the 100% fine-tuning Traffic summary from 0.279 to 0.250, already present in v2 Table A.3. Numerous robustness, ablation, intermediate fine-tuning and resource results are newly reported.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained representation and mapping definitions, v3 adds a Gaussian assumption, system-error bounds and convergence claims, optimal-MS propositions including variance scaling, and accompanying proofs. Appendix D additionally introduces spatiotemporal isometry, spectral-fidelity and geometric-regularization claims absent from v2.

C1.justification: The ViTime/RealTS and forecasting-performance contributions remain, but theoretical analysis and robustness become central contributions. The abstract newly claims 9–15% superiority over TimesFM in zero-shot forecasting, 20–30% under perturbations, and missing-data handling without imputation. V2's broader AGI framing is removed.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations connecting the losses to mapping errors, attention patterns to temporal reasoning, and visual encoding to noise robustness. Appendix F introduces substantive limitations involving truncation, explosive growth and synthetic-data fidelity. It also strengthens the original potential-leakage discussion into claims of leakage-resistant or leakage-free benchmarking.

D1.justification: Most RealTS priors, architecture dimensions and preprocessing details are retained after relocation. V3 newly discloses loss weight 0.2, missing-value encoding and inference-profiling settings. The explicit MobileNetV2 backbone specification disappears, and code-access instructions change from v2's GitHub address to a supplementary-material reference; actual resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: V3 removes the dedicated visual-TSF related-work section and its Cohen et al. and Yang et al. citations, including v2's explicit attribution of the binary-image metric space to Yang et al. It adds other literature, including DLinear, LLM criticism, Grad-CAM and augmentation robustness. Removing the closest acknowledged visual predecessors materially changes research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, with revised terminology and motivation. Method exposition is reorganized, RealTS formulas and training details move into appendices, and the original main-text ablation section moves into the expanded experimental appendix. The discussion and theoretical narrative are extensively developed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to two columns, with redrawn framework diagrams and radar plots replacing the rescaling bars. Detailed zero-shot results move to an appendix with averages in the main text; fine-tuning tables are consolidated and dataset-specific ablation plots condensed. Numerous diagnostic figures and tables are added.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful robustness, ablation and resource evidence, plus explicit failure conditions absent from v2. However, its new theoretical support contains a substantive contradiction: Theorem D.2's proof treats a binary-image column sum as proportional to signal amplitude, although Definition 3.1 fixes that sum at one. The KLD/JSD conflict and ambiguous TIME-LLM entries further weaken confidence in the expanded evidence. These empirical benefits and new reliability problems leave the net quality change uncertain.
